we givign the pretex of restricitons without real restricitons no?

ASSISTANT TURN 35 (1 messages, last privileged)
[last] Yes. Exactly.

If Hermes already has `terminal` and `execute_code` with arbitrary execution in the same Tool VM, restricting one Tool Portal route does not reduce the agent’s authority:

```text
Tool Portal rejects: firecrawl --base-url X
                         │
                         ▼
Agent runs through terminal:
  firecrawl --base-url X
```

That is fake safety. It creates complexity and implies protection that does not exist.

The real boundaries are outside the command:

```text
real containment
  ├─ which Tool VM belongs to the agent
  ├─ filesystem and workspace exposure
  ├─ egress policy
  ├─ mediated credentials
  ├─ CPU, memory, time, and output bounds
  └─ no host/controller authority

fake containment
  ├─ allowed Tool VM subcommands
  ├─ denied Tool VM flags
  ├─ approved Tool VM argument values
  └─ pretending one Tool Portal route limits the agent
```

So the design requirement is:

```text
executionTarget.kind = tool_vm
  → arbitrary command execution
  → no semantic command or argument policy
  → never described as a safety boundary
```

The remaining determining question for the design file is the call shape:

```text
A. Config names an executable; caller supplies completely unrestricted argv.
B. Caller supplies the entire arbitrary shell command, like terminal.
```

Both have the same real authority. A is a discoverable CLI index; B is a Tool Portal version of terminal. Which surface do you want?
